entries.notes: Kind typo, with no anchor or refutation, so there is nothing to answer. All three edits are editorial and change no meaning. (1) l.202 now writes the pair policy first, as v2's definition does (l.165: a star forward policy, then the star outflow) and as EGF.GenerativeFlow does (fields `policy` then `outflow`). Every other ordered pair of a policy and an outflow in v2's text is already policy first: l.188, 279, 311, 367, 372, 376, 437, 825, 830, 880, 952, 961, 965. (2) l.437 'bounded as follows:' is grammar only. Corollary 3.10's content (EGF-C1's negative-part delta, EGF-C5's reversed KL) is untouched. (3) l.465: the loss display's cap is now t_{\text{max}}, the same as the buffer step (l.459) and the m-gloss (l.467). Under icml2025.sty's times, \max was set in the operator font, so the cap now renders in one font throughout Algorithm 1. pdftotext shows only a small spacing change in the display. The sum's range and Algorithm 1's estimate (C-59, C-65) are unchanged. No hypothesis was added, which agrees with added_hypotheses [].

Kind typo, with no refutation. Captions (l.1279, l.1326, l.1385, l.1431): 'the spin wheel' adds an article, and 'four circles' matches C-44 and C-62's 'two spirals' (l.1493, l.1539). The dataset files (ablation/4Circles/, star_*.png) are unchanged, and no other text names these datasets. The series sentences (l.784, l.882) now state the remark's hypothesis in the remark's words. The remark (l.897, C-21's text) reads: 'If $\lambda$ itself is invariant, $\lambda\ForwardPolicyStar=\lambda$, and $\ForwardPolicyStar$ is summably $L^2$-mixing with $\widehat\lambda=\lambda$'. l.749 (C-61) has the same clause. The Lean anchors take exactly this hypothesis: mixingCoeff π lam lam (λ̂ = λ), [IsMarkovKernel π], [IsFiniteMeasure lam] and hinv : lam.bind π = lam. mixingCoeff_self_add_le gives γ_{m+n} ≤ γ_m γ_n. tsum_mixingCoeff_self_ne_top_iff gives Σγ_n < ∞ ⟺ ∃N, γ_N < 1, and hasExponentialL2Decay_iff gives the geometric decay. λ finite is Theorem B.1's setting (l.880) and Section 2's 'finite background measure' (l.165). So the two edited sentences are now Lean's hypothesis word for word. Their conclusion ('gives the outflow as a convergent series', i.e. the remark's) is unchanged and is covered by C-21's anchors (with bounded densities, general ones after truncation). The clause changes no meaning: under 'λ invariant' it is equivalent to Definition 3.3's summability. For a finite λ̂, C-72's chain proves it: isKernelErgodic_of_isSummablyL2Mixing makes π ergodic for λ, and ae_eq_const_of_densityAction_eq makes dλ̂/dλ constant, so λ̂ = cλ and γ_n(λ̂) = c·γ_n(λ). One caveat on the register's finding, not on the paper: ae_eq_const_of_densityAction_eq needs dλ̂/dλ ∈ L¹(λ), i.e. λ̂ finite, which neither Definition 3.3 nor EGF.IsSummablyL2Mixing requires. An infinite λ̂ is excluded only by an unformalized step: γ_0 < ∞ forces dλ̂/dλ to be essentially bounded when H ≠ ∅, and when H = ∅ every γ_n is 0. The edit writes the proved form, so the paper no longer depends on that step. This narrowing is a gain. Two readings were checked and are harmless. (a) 'λ invariant and λ̂ = λ' is redundant, since Definition 3.3's λ̂ is invariant. The remark uses the same wording. (b) At l.882, λ̂ also names Theorem B.1's measure. With λ invariant both readings take λ̂ = λ, and ergodicity for λ follows from summable mixing. The clause is C-21's listed added hypothesis ('lambda invariant (lambda-hat = lambda) for the series remark'), restated where the remark is cited, so it is not a hypothesis new to the paper. added_hypotheses [] is therefore consistent. The other mixing sentences need no clause: l.292, l.304 and l.793 claim no series, and l.749 has it already.

answers.question: Is each edit exactly its entry's fix, with no change of meaning?
answers.answer: Yes, all nine, checked character by character. The two 'with $\widehat\lambda=\lambda$' insertions now state C-21's remark's hypothesis, and so the anchors' hypothesis: mixingCoeff π lam lam with lam.bind π = lam and lam finite, in EGF.mixingCoeff_self_add_le and EGF.tsum_mixingCoeff_self_ne_top_iff. Under 'λ invariant' the clause is equivalent to Definition 3.3. The equivalence is formalized for a finite λ̂ and follows for an infinite one by a short unformalized γ_0 argument. Either way the edited text claims no more than Lean proves.
